gloss: a mountain of; huge piles of; an enormous amount of

definitions.gloss: a mountain of; piled high; an enormous amount of
definitions.explanation: A simile likening a large quantity to a mountain. Used with concrete things stacked up ({書類|しょるい}, {洗濯物|せんたくもの}) and with abstract ones (work, complaints).

examples.japanese: ⟦{宿題|しゅくだい}→宿題：00812_shukudai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{山|やま}のよう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: I have a mountain of homework.

examples.japanese: ⟦{机|つくえ}→机：00762_tsukue⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{上|うえ}→上：00682_ue⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{書類|しょるい}→書類：01103_shorui⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{山|やま}のよう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{積|つ}まれている→積む：02294_tsumu⟧。
examples.english: Documents are piled like a mountain on the desk.

examples.japanese: ⟦{連休|れんきゅう}{明|あ}け→連休明け：17704_renkyuuake⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦メール→メール：04435_meeru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{山|やま}のよう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{届|とど}いていて→届く：00899_todoku⟧、⟦{処理|しょり}→処理：03251_shori⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{半日|はんにち}→半日：27978_hannichi⟧⟦かかった→かかる：00711_kakaru⟧。
examples.english: After the long weekend, a mountain of emails had arrived, and it took half a day to process them.

notes:
Modifier built from ⟦{山|やま}→山：02168_yama⟧ (mountain) + ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧よう (looking like). Used adverbially with ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ ({山|やま}のよう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧) or as a noun modifier with な.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- With ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧: as an adverb modifying a verb ({山|やま}のよう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧、⟦{積|つ}まれている→積む：02294_tsumu⟧、⟦{届|とど}く→届く：00899_todoku⟧)
- With な: as a noun modifier ({山|やま}のような⟦{量|りょう}→量：03799_ryou⟧)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{仕事|しごと}→仕事：00480_shigoto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{山|やま}のよう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧: to have a mountain of work
- {山|やま}のような⟦{書類|しょるい}→書類：01103_shorui⟧: a mountain of paperwork
- ⟦{不満|ふまん}→不満：02497_fuman⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{山|やま}のよう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧: to have a mountain of complaints

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {山|やま}ほど: 'as much as a mountain' — interchangeable in most contexts, slightly more casual
- ⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧: a lot — neutral and lacks the vivid 'piled high' image
- ⟦{膨大|ぼうだい}→膨大：08997_boudai⟧な: enormous — more formal, used for abstract quantities like data
